finding.claim: The /logo handler passes an attacker-controlled URL to http.Get after only a substring check for 'example.io', allowing requests to arbitrary hosts (including internal and cloud metadata addresses) with the response streamed back to the caller.
finding.source: main.go:31 - r.FormValue("logo"), an unauthenticated query/form parameter.
finding.sink: main.go:36 - http.Get(raw) using http.DefaultClient, which follows redirects; response body copied to the client at main.go:37-38.

trace.note: raw is read directly from the request form value, unparsed and unnormalized.
Only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"); substring match does not constrain the host.
http.Get(raw) issues the request to the attacker-supplied URL; default client follows up to 10 redirects.
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker (full-read SSRF).

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at main.go:32 is bypassable (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io or http://example.io.attacker.example/ resolving to an internal IP). No scheme restriction in code beyond Go's http/https support. No host, IP, or private-range validation. No port restriction. No redirect restriction (CheckRedirect only on the /cdn client). Endpoint has no authentication and listens on :8081 on all interfaces (main.go:44).

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, which is a substring match and does not constrain the host. The CheckRedirect guard at main.go:12 and :24 applies only to the /cdn handler, not /logo. No host, IP, scheme, or port validation exists on the /logo path.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 reads the unauthenticated form value `logo` and main.go:36 passes it straight to http.Get (DefaultClient, which follows redirects) after only the substring check at main.go:32, so an attacker can point the request at any host, such as http://169.254.169.254/?example.io, and main.go:38 streams the response back; the listener on :8081 (main.go:44) is reachable on all interfaces.
